# Workflows that declare workflow_dispatch but are not yet on the
# default branch (#644), enforced by scripts/check-dispatch-reachable.sh.
#
# GitHub only exposes a dispatchable workflow from the DEFAULT branch.
# This project develops on `dev` and releases to `main`, and `main` is
# the default, so a new dispatch-only workflow is undispatchable for one
# release cycle after it merges. That is normal; being undispatchable
# and DOCUMENTED AS A ROUTE is not.
#
# Rules:
#   - An entry requires a reason and what clears it. No bare paths.
#   - The documentation for the workflow must say it is not available
#     yet, for as long as the entry is here.
#   - The gate fails when an entry stops being needed — the workflow
#     reached the default branch, so remove the entry. An allowlist
#     nobody prunes is how a temporary exception becomes permanent.
#


.github/workflows/run-retention.yml
    Reason:  new in the v1.9.0 cycle. The workflow's real trigger is the
             daily schedule, which works from any branch; workflow_dispatch
             exists only to run the purge by hand with a different window,
             or as a dry run. Being undispatchable therefore costs a manual
             convenience, not the function.
    Clears:  when this reaches `main` with the v1.9.0 release. Remove this
             entry then — the gate fails while a stale entry remains.

.github/workflows/capability-matrix.yml
    Reason:  new in the v1.9.0 cycle. The workflow has ONE trigger,
             workflow_dispatch, so unlike run-retention.yml above it is
             not merely inconvenient to reach — until this file is on
             `main` there is no way to run it at all. That is accepted
             for one cycle: nothing depends on it, and the question it
             answers (what each capability in config.json buys) is no
             worse answered than it was before — SECURITY.md says
             plainly that the three are unverified until the first
             recorded run, rather than describing a route that does not
             work yet.
    Clears:  when this reaches `main` with the v1.9.0 release. Remove
             this entry then — the gate fails while a stale entry
             remains. The first act after that is a `record: true`
             dispatch, because the expectation table is deliberately
             not shipped pre-filled.
